line: Crowley gives Binah the number 3 and Saturn, and his own lists disagree about Saturn; Jung calls Binah the root in which the tree of life is rooted.

sections.title: Crowley's number 3
sections.line: The third sephira is Binah, Understanding, and the Threes are referred to it.

quotes.quote: shows the third Sephira, Binah, Understanding, as not yet formulated
These cards are referred to Binah; in each of them is expressed the symbolism of Understanding.
Binah, the Great Mother, here rules the realm of Air.

sections.title: Saturn and the Moon
sections.line: Crowley gives Binah Saturn, and in another aspect the Moon.

quotes.quote: Binah, the Great Sea, is the Moon in one aspect, but Saturn in another;

sections.title: Where Crowley's lists disagree
sections.line: The Universe list gives its third item as Saturn with the Abyss, and Diagram 5 puts Saturn in the place of the non-existent Daath. Both are Crowley's statements; the site keeps the conflict visible.

quotes.quote: Saturn. The Abyss. This is represented by Herschel,

sections.title: Jung's root of the tree
sections.line: Jung calls Binah the upper Sefira, in which the tree of life is rooted, and the source of the middle line that brings life down. He does not number it.

quotes.quote: in Binah is rooted the tree of life
which was as it were the trunk of the Sefiroth system, it brought life down to earth from Binah
